the_pre_batch_state.★_how_these_were_taken: `git hash-object --no-filters -w <path>` per file, before any edit of this batch. `--no-filters` hashes the bytes on disk rather than the end-of-line-normalised form, so a line-ending change could not hide inside an equal hash. Each blob is written into the object database, so every pre-batch file is recoverable at `git cat-file blob <hash>` whatever happens afterwards.

the_post_batch_state: NOT RENDERED — deliberately, and the ground is at `the_start_state_stop` above.  Every file named in `the_pre_batch_state` is unchanged on disk, which is re-checkable by running `git hash-object --no-filters` over the same paths and comparing with the blobs recorded there.

the_verdict.the_render: NOT PERFORMED.  A STOP the dispatch names fired before the write, and it is a start-state condition this batch did not cause and does not repair.

the_measurement.★_what_was_measured_and_why_it_is_this_a: The prediction is a claim about what the EXTENSION does, so it is tested by running the PRE-batch generator and the POST-batch generator over the SAME sources, in memory, and comparing what each would render.  A disk comparison cannot answer it, because the packs on disk were already stale before this batch began — see `the_start_state_stop` below — so a difference there would confound source drift with the effect of the extension.  Nothing was rendered to any pack directory and no manifest was written.
the_measurement.how_to_re_run_it: `git show f54995c092:tools/audit/gen_derivation_boot_pack.py` gives the pre-batch generator; both it and the file at HEAD-of-working-tree are executed with `__file__` set to the real tool path so their own ROOT resolves to the repository, and `build()` is called on each. the_start_state_stop.★_the_consequence_for_TASK_6: Task 6's three conditions cannot all hold from this start state, and the conflict is not a matter of judgment: `--check` GREEN requires the two existing packs to be re-rendered from the grown sources, and `byte-identical to their pre-batch state` forbids exactly that.  §4 of the dispatch settles which way it falls — *a difference anywhere in either existing pack is a STOP, not a thing to explain afterwards* — so the STOP fires BEFORE the write, which is why the pre-batch state was pinned first.  NOTHING WAS WRITTEN to either existing pack, to the new pack directory, or to the manifest: `write_all` writes the manifest for every subject on any invocation, so even `--subject l0-l1` would have moved the two existing subjects' manifest entries, which the same task forbids in terms.  Refreshing those packs changes what a future blind deriving session reads, which is a behaviour change and the user's to ratify (#14).
